title: FAMILIA Chobani Cardiovascular Health Program
summary: This study builds upon the overarching hypothesis of the FAMILIA studies: early and repeated exposure to structured cardiovascular health promotion programs can shape long-term behavior and reduce lifetime cardiovascular risk. FAMILIA Cardiovascular Chobani Health Program specifically targets adolescents, evaluating whether a 4-month after-school intervention can act as a behavioral booster for those previously exposed to health promotion in early childhood, while also evaluating its impact in adolescents with no prior exposure. A secondary objective is to assess the sustainability of changes in mindset and behavior, while also assessing whether physiological health factors change over a two-year follow-up period. To complement the adolescent's findings, the study includes a parallel assessment of progression of subclinical atherosclerosis in parents who received a similar intervention a decade earlier as part of FAMILIA Project I. In FAMILIA Project I, prevalence of subclinical atherosclerosis was evaluated by vascular ultrasound and its associations with sociodemographic factors have been already published. Subclinical atherosclerosis in parents serves as a marker of long-term cardiovascular risk, offering insight into how risk may accumulate over time and potentially mirror future trajectories in their children.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

• Adolescents 11-16 years old who either participated in the FAMILIA Project in preschool or who attend an after-school program running the educational program.

Exclusion criteria for adolescents

* Parent or legal guardian does not provide informed consent.
* Adolescent is unable to complete study assessments, even with assistance.

Exclusion criteria for adults:

• Unable to provide informed consent to participate in the study.
